clue.text: Possible end for famed car

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the tail of the following word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of famed

explanation.surface: Speculation about how a celebrated motor might finally be scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' marks the definition as one example: the answer is one possible car, not a synonym for car.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford is a well-known American motor manufacturer, so its vehicles are an example of a car make.

clue.text: Linked computers: alien seizing number in that place

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so one piece wraps around the rest
one item sitting in another means it is placed inside that word

blocks.note: ET is the film's extra-terrestrial, the usual crossword alien
N is the standard abbreviation for number
a synonym: that place is there

explanation.surface: A sci-fi scene of networked machines with an alien grabbing a number somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: the number goes inside 'that place' first, and the alien then wraps around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the common cabled technology for joining computers into a local network.

clue.text: Tarty lass I played in classic sex comedy

indicators.note: something played is performed in a new way, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An actress confessing she played a floozy in a racy old stage comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Aristophanes' play has the women of Greece withhold sex to end a war, so the surface's theatre setting is the real one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysistrata is an ancient Greek comedy by Aristophanes built around a sex strike.

clue.text: Apprentice overlooking one new sign of damage

indicators.note: to overlook something is to leave it out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: to indent someone is to bind them as an apprentice by a contract
the Roman numeral for one
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A trainee fails to notice a fresh scratch on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apprentice' is used as a verb, to indent or indenture; INDENT then loses I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A dent is a hollow knocked into a surface, a visible mark that something has been hit.

clue.text: Old King's skill reduced damage

indicators.note: something reduced is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a synonym: an art is a skill
a synonym: to hurt is to damage

explanation.surface: A former monarch's abilities have been diminished by injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur is the legendary early British king of the Round Table, so an ancient monarch.

clue.text: Left in awful desert sun - what will finally happen?

indicators.note: one item placed in others is put among those letters
something awful is in a dreadful state, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned under a brutal desert sun wonders how it will all end.
explanation.definitionFit: End results are final outcomes, the eventual consequences of a process.

clue.text: Second way lady loses heart, to a large degree

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so the central letters are dropped

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
ST, street, is a common way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Briefly, a woman becomes largely discouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: Mostly means for the most part, which is the same as to a large degree or extent.

clue.text: Direction always required in police operation

indicators.note: something needed in an operation sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
a sting is an undercover operation to trap criminals

explanation.surface: Guidance that a police raid always needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Steering is guiding the course of something, giving it direction.

clue.text: Feels answers misplaced about American perception of individuality

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong positions, so these letters are rearranged
about means around, so the other letters go round one piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
A is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant senses their answers have gone astray around an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-awareness is conscious knowledge of one's own character and feelings as a distinct person.

clue.text: Advantage initially held before unfortunate battle

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: a synonym: an edge is an advantage
the first letter of held
ill as in ill luck, unlucky

explanation.surface: An early lead was squandered ahead of an ill-fated fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgehill, in Warwickshire, was the first pitched battle of the English Civil War in 1642.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgehill names a 1642 English Civil War engagement, so it is one particular battle.

clue.text: Desire to see promotion of small casual garb

indicators.note: a promotion moves something up, so the letter for small is shifted forward in the word

blocks.note: a thirst for something is a desire

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a sale on small sizes of relaxed clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the clothing-label abbreviation for small; in THIRST it moves up from fifth place to second.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shirt is an informal collarless top, a standard item of relaxed everyday clothing.

clue.text: Playing of disc starts to exhibit this keyboard instrument

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: a DJ gives a record a spin when playing it
the first letters of exhibit and this

explanation.surface: Putting on a record opens a show featuring a particular keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord-like instrument played from a keyboard.

clue.text: Tinder alternative - a lot of green stuff burning internally

indicators.note: something internal sits inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: as in a pound a kilo, meaning per
a salad is a heap of leaves
a light or fire that is burning is on

explanation.surface: Instead of a dating app, someone sets fire to a heap of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of green stuff' looks like money (dollar bills are green) but is a salad. Tinder is a dating app.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal ad is a lonely-hearts notice in a paper, the older way to find a date than a dating app.

clue.text: Saw mops - hair, flopping

indicators.note: something flopping falls about loosely, so these letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sees shaggy heads of hair hanging limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saw is a traditional proverb, and an aphorism is a pithy saying of general truth.

clue.text: One getting nowhere giving people the finger?

definitions.text: One getting nowhere giving people the finger?

blocks.clueFragment: One getting nowhere giving people the finger?
blocks.note: surface reading: a frustrated person making a rude gesture at others

blocks.clueFragment: One getting nowhere giving people the finger?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a roadside traveller stuck in one place, holding out a thumb to passing drivers

explanation.walkthrough: Getting nowhere is literal, standing still at the roadside; the finger is the raised thumb asking for a lift, not an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitchhiker travels by soliciting free rides from passing motorists, traditionally by sticking out a thumb.

clue.text: Amusing comments about rule or legal document

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: wit is clever, funny remarks
R is an abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: Jokes made about a regulation or a legal paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal court order in written form, issued under legal authority.

clue.text: Prone to hold Arab in a separate area

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: prone to and apt to both mean inclined to
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A man inclined to detain an Arab in his own quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart describes being kept separately, at a distance from others.

clue.text: Fellow's sick - the maximum one'll tolerate

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
a synonym: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A man is unwell and has reached his limit of tolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the idiom 'I have had my fill', meaning as much as I can stand.
explanation.definitionFit: One's fill is the full amount one can take, the limit of what can be endured.

clue.text: Number in favour of drink as well, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the spoken words stand for a differently spelt answer

blocks.note: for means supporting
tea is a drink
too means also

explanation.surface: Someone backs a drink, and another one too.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, the three words give the number, which is also the famous answer to everything in The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty-two is a whole number, the sum of forty and two.

clue.text: Time to keep quiet, beset by further financial burden

indicators.note: something beset is surrounded on all sides, so the first pieces go inside

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to gag someone is to keep them quiet
a synonym: further means more

explanation.surface: Being silenced for a while, besieged by yet more money worries.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortgage is a large home loan, a long-term debt that weighs on household finances.

clue.text: A market rising with investment by university, providing shock

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upward, so the letters run backwards
an investment is something put in, so a letter is placed inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a mart is a market
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A recovering market backed by a college's money provides a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a deeply distressing experience, an emotional or physical shock.

clue.text: Tailless leporid, donkey and badger

indicators.note: without a tail, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: leporids are the hare and rabbit family
a synonym: an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A menagerie of a bob-tailed hare, a donkey and a badger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' sits among the animals as if a third creature, but it is the verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them persistently, which is to harass them.

clue.text: Happy to snare undisciplined stars

indicators.note: to snare is to trap, so one piece is caught inside the other

blocks.note: gay in its older sense of merry
lax means loose and unruly

explanation.surface: Pleased to catch out some celebrities who behave badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast system of stars; it is also used for a gathering of famous people.

clue.text: Agreement to secure volume for Frenchman?

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: yes expresses agreement
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: A deal that guarantees a book for someone from France.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is by example: this is one French man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Yves is a common French given name, as in the designer Yves Saint Laurent.

clue.text: Instructive end to overture, fading, with one forte interrupting

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
to interrupt is to break into the middle, so a piece goes inside

blocks.note: the final letter of overture
the Roman numeral for one
f is the musical marking for forte, loud
a dying sound is fading away

explanation.surface: A musical piece's prelude dies away, then a loud passage cuts in, which is enlightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Edifying means morally or intellectually improving, so something that instructs or uplifts.

clue.text: Standard number affixed to room

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
RM is the abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: A regular numeral stuck on a hotel door.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual or expected level, a benchmark or standard.

clue.text: Head of Hall without members having no influence

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that is used

blocks.note: the first letter of Hall
arms are limbs, or members, so lacking them is being armless

explanation.surface: A club chairman with no members left has no power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' suggests a club's membership but means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harmless has no capacity to hurt, so it exerts no damaging effect or influence.

clue.text: King Lear?

blocks.note: first meaning: the name of eight English monarchs
second meaning: the forename of the Victorian nonsense poet Lear, the question mark showing it is a first name by example

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue is Shakespeare's tragedy, but it splits into a royal name and the limerick writer of The Owl and the Pussycat.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward was borne by eight English monarchs and was also the given name of the poet Lear.
